findings.title: Redirect tests still bypass the production urllib redirect handler
findings.criterion_ref: RC9-T10 requires the automated suites to “genuinely exercise ... redirect denial”; the review instructions specifically call out fixtures that bypass the production call site.
findings.trigger: The production `_default_opener` stops invoking `redirect_validator` before `super().redirect_request`, or invokes it after the redirected request begins.
findings.consequence: All advertised redirect tests remain green while production can again follow an excess or downgraded redirect before validation. The suite therefore does not provide the required executable regression proof for the repaired boundary.
findings.evidence: Production wiring exists only in `runtime/langgraph_factory/egress.py` lines 447–477, especially lines 458–464. No test invokes `_default_opener`. `tests/runtime/test_plan26_egress.py` lines 271–286 supplies a canned opener that independently calls the callback, and lines 349–368 supplies another synthetic opener that manually models request order. The D06B composition test at `test_plan26_deterministic_nodes.py` lines 456–463 also injects a lambda opener with no redirect. Removing or moving the production callback at egress.py line 462 would leave all these tests passing.

observations: The round-1 history exactly matches my prior verdict and three findings.

RC9-QA-001 is resolved: production D06B now consumes `(body, receipt)`, verifies the body hash, persists content-addressed bytes, and the test composes the actual D06B and SourceRetriever implementations.

The runtime implementation portion of RC9-QA-002 is resolved: the urllib handler calls validation before constructing the redirect request, checks the bound before the excess hop, and revalidates scheme, host, port, DNS addresses, and final URL.
RC9-QA-003 is resolved: missing Content-Type now produces `content_type_missing`.

All 23 bundle-listed hashes matched. The validator returned `valid:true`; scanners were clean; the recomputed suites produced 294, 492/1 skipped/140 subtests, 62/27 subtests, 18/234 deselected, and 175 passes as recorded. The v7, modified-v7, v8, baseline live, and baseline HEAD hashes also matched.

The failed v1 bundle retains its exact prior hash under `deprecated/`, but `manifest.v2.json` still records its path as `rc9_review_bundle.v1.md` at the rc9 root. The bytes remain readable, so this does not defeat the stated preservation criterion.
reasoning: The three runtime defects from round 1 are repaired. I did not invent findings against the corrected tuple, redirect, or Content-Type behavior. One threshold defect survives specifically in the automated-proof criterion: every redirect test replaces the production opener and manually invokes the callback, so none can detect regression at the exact urllib hook that must enforce pre-follow validation.
